articles.title: Metrolink Tram Disruption Expected Between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale in August
articles.excerpt: Track renewals will cause tram disruption between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale on August 15 and 16, requiring passengers to plan ahead for alternative travel arrangements.
articles.content_html:
Track renewals will cause disruption to Metrolink tram services between Manchester Victoria and Rochdale this August. Passengers who use the Rochdale line should prepare for changes to their travel plans.

No trams will operate from Manchester Victoria to Rochdale Town Centre on August 15 and 16. This interruption is part of ongoing maintenance work aimed at improving service reliability.

Passengers are advised to seek alternative travel arrangements during this period. Further details regarding service changes can be found on the Metrolink website.

The track renewals are expected to enhance the overall efficiency of the tram network, but may cause inconvenience for those relying on this route.

articles.title: Rochdale Local Plan Moves Forward with Public Consultation
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan, outlining development strategies until 2039, is set for public consultation after council approval. It includes plans for new housing and transport hubs.
articles.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 31 July 2026 at 12:28. 2 source updates have been combined into this article.

The Rochdale Local Plan, outlining development strategies until 2039, is set for public consultation after council approval. It includes plans for new housing and transport hubs.

Latest update

A council meeting on July 28 approved the borough's Local Plan, which will guide development and housing strategies until 2039. The plan includes the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes to local transport stations. Following revisions to a 175-page document, the plan is set to enter public consultation before its expected formal adoption in 2027.

Originally, the plan mandated that new housing developments include 20 per cent affordable housing. However, this requirement has been reduced to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this adjustment does not reflect a diminished commitment to affordable housing, noting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding previous targets.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy that includes the Places for Everyone plan, which aims to build around 175,000 homes across Greater Manchester over the next two decades. The Rochdale borough is also set to benefit from the Atom Valley scheme, which envisions 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs, alongside the development of the Sustainable Materials and Manufacturing Centre in Kingsway.

The plan places a strong emphasis on housing and transport, with a focus on reconfiguring land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create vibrant communities around stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a new Slattocks station, enhancing local economic growth and community engagement.

Earlier developments

A plan that will shape Rochdale’s future over the next 13 years has moved closer to implementation following approval from council leaders. The Rochdale Local Plan outlines how the borough will develop until 2039, including the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes to local transport hubs.

The council has refined a 175-page document, which will now enter a public consultation phase. The formal adoption of the plan is anticipated later in 2027. Initially, the plan required that 20 per cent of new housing developments be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this adjustment does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, noting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding the previous target.

Housing is a central focus of the plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone initiative. This strategy, adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils, aims to construct around 175,000 homes across the region over the next two decades. The Local Plan is expected to attract investment and facilitate major redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is a key component of the plan, aiming to transform areas around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This strategy includes enhancements to stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a proposed new station at Slattocks. The plan also incorporates improved walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to boost the local economy and enhance the quality of life for residents.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Central Park Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Central Park tram stop towards Rochdale is currently out of service, affecting step-free access for passengers.
articles.content_html:
A lift at Central Park tram stop, which serves passengers travelling towards Rochdale via Oldham, is currently out of service. The disruption began on Wednesday, 29 July, at 5:26pm and will continue until further notice.

Customers travelling towards Oldham can access the Manchester-bound platform via lift from The Gateway and then use the track crossing to reach the Oldham-bound platform. The lift's unavailability may cause inconvenience for those requiring step-free access.

Transport for Greater Manchester has issued an apology for the disruption and is advising passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. For more information, visit the Transport for Greater Manchester website.

articles.title: Rochdale's Local Plan to Shape Future with Thousands of New Homes
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's Local Plan aims to build nearly 11,000 new homes and transform transport hubs by 2039, with a council meeting set to discuss the proposal on July 28.
articles.content_html:
A council meeting on July 28 will discuss the Rochdale Local Plan, which aims to shape the borough's future until 2039. The plan includes the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes around transport hubs.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy called Places for Everyone, which has been adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils. This strategy envisions around 175,000 new homes across the city region over the next two decades, with Rochdale expected to see substantial investment and redevelopment.

Key elements of the Local Plan include the Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy, which focuses on reconfiguring land around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This initiative aims to create vibrant spaces for living, working, and leisure, enhancing the local economy.

The plan also addresses various topics such as climate and energy, economic growth, housing, and sustainable transport. Rochdale is identified as the principal town centre, with ongoing regeneration efforts including the £20 million redevelopment of the Grade-I listed Rochdale Town Hall, completed in 2024. The Local Plan is expected to push forward the borough's ambitions for growth and development.

The vision for Rochdale includes transforming the borough's stations into centres for change, with a focus on creating community spaces and improving transport links. The Local Plan will be discussed further at the council meeting, where it is anticipated to move to the next phase before formal adoption.
